publicationStmt.publisher: eLiebermann: An Online Dictionary of Pre-Conquest English Law

div.head: About eLiebermann
div.p: Felix Liebermann's Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen (Halle, 1903–1916) is the standard edition of the laws of England before the Norman Conquest. Its three volumes give the texts, a dictionary (Wörterbuch, volume 2, part 1), a glossary of legal and historical terms (Rechts- und Sachglossar, volume 2, part 2), and commentary (volume 3).

The Wörterbuch is dense. Entries are in German, cite passages by law code and section, and note manuscript variants by single-letter sigla, all heavily abbreviated. eLiebermann makes it searchable and links every abbreviation to its expansion, so the dictionary can be read by anyone working on early English law.

div.head: How entries are made
div.p: The team transcribes entries from the printed volume into Word, keeping Liebermann's bold, italic and superscript, since the formatting carries meaning: a superscript L or F marks Latin and French words, italics are Liebermann's German, and roman type is the language of the laws. Each entry is turned into a TEI file, the standard format for scholarly texts, and law codes and abbreviations are linked automatically. Editors then check each entry, and add English translations and links to the Bosworth-Toller Anglo-Saxon Dictionary, the Dictionary of Old English and Wiktionary.
Nothing is published until an editor adds it to the site, and every entry links to the page of the printed volume it comes from, so readers can check it.

div.head: Citing eLiebermann
div.p: Please cite the entry you used and its page in Liebermann, for example: “bocland”, eLiebermann: An Online Dictionary of Pre-Conquest English Law, https://notamitchell.github.io/law/entry.html?id=bocland (after F. Liebermann, Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen, vol. 2.1, p. 26).

The printed edition is reissued as: Liebermann, F. (Ed.). (2015). Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen: Herausgegeben im Auftrage der Savigny-Stiftung (Cambridge Library Collection - Medieval History). Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. doi:10.1017/CBO9781316225127

div.head: Code and data
div.p: The site's code and every entry are on GitHub at github.com/notamitchell/law. The entries are plain TEI XML files, free to reuse.
